scope: Observed local compiler, generated programs, fuzzing and editor packages; actual desktop and remote CI recorded separately
clippy: all targets, fuzzing feature, -D warnings passed

traversal_native.scope: Actual final compiler-generated C11 under GCC/Clang ASan/UBSan
cases_per_compiler: signed keys, exact associations/coverage, growth and shifted collision chains
copied boolean/String and borrowed object/enum/interface/nested-collection values
generic headers, evaluated-once borrowed getter, receiver-derived borrowed return
nested shared loops and continue/break/return ownership cleanup

fuzz.scope: Real bounded local development campaigns; final source commit additionally runs remote CI fuzzing. Finite runs are not a safety proof

applied: List/map binding and receiver rules share one checked contract
Existing block/while flow and cleanup reused
Storage expressions stay compiler-only; C layout knowledge remains in collection backend
Borrowed map representation shared between direct traversal and ordinary accessors
Capacity captured once under invariant root loan; no iterator allocation, owner copies or key rehashing
Read-only catalog queries separate scans from commands; ordered persistence unchanged
No predicate framework or redundant validation pass added
tradeoffs: Internal typed IR expressions require pass-specific handlers while sharing an authoritative vocabulary
Catalog.entriesRef exposes standard collection type as a read-only capability because no opaque iterator view exists; bucket layout and mutable access remain hidden
Mutating put/tryRemove commands return transferred owners rather than enforcing void-only command-query separation

remote_ci.scope: Exact executable source commit; subsequent evidence-only publication changes docs/checksums only
hosted_warnings: Existing actions target deprecated Node 20 and were forced to Node 24

publication: Curated portable sources only; historical evidence labels preserved; no workstation paths, credentials, process IDs, profiles, caches or private proof locations
